articles.title: Signal restricts screenshots to combat AI surveillance threats
articles.summary: Messaging app Signal is limiting users' ability to capture screenshots on both its Android and iOS platforms. The move comes as the company attempts to address growing concerns surrounding AI surveillance and data privacy.

articles.title: Trump calls reported FBI database hack 'not good'
articles.summary: The FBI is reportedly investigating a security breach involving the National Crime Information Center. Former President Donald Trump publicly addressed the incident, describing the reported database hack as a negative development for the agency.

articles.title: Actor licenses AI face to startup, sparking Hollywood debate
articles.summary: An actor has licensed an artificial intelligence version of his face to a microdrama startup, mirroring a popular trend in China. Industry experts are now questioning the potential long-term consequences if this practice becomes widespread in Hollywood.

articles.title: Alaska governor-elect known for thousands of Wikipedia edits
articles.summary: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, the governor-elect of Alaska, has drawn attention for his extensive background as an online contributor. Before taking office, he successfully made more than 13,000 edits on the crowdsourced encyclopedia Wikipedia.

articles.title: Startup sues Apple in India over contact sharing
articles.summary: A United States-based startup is taking legal action against Apple in India over a tap-to-share contacts feature. The company is seeking $162 million in damages alongside an injunction that could impact iPhone and Apple Watch imports.

articles.title: Spotify founder backs AI researcher's fusion startup
articles.summary: Spotify founder Daniel Ek is investing in Europa Fusion, a newly established fusion power startup created by an artificial intelligence researcher. The company aims to develop advanced clean energy solutions backed by prominent tech funding.

articles.title: AI and human mathematicians propose Riemann hypothesis solutions
articles.summary: Mathematicians are reacting to a recent artificial intelligence-driven result that claims to solve the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis. Interestingly, a competing solution has also been put forward by a human researcher, creating a fascinating dual milestone.

articles.title: Super-hot rock geothermal energy could power data centers
articles.summary: New geothermal energy startups are betting on innovative technologies to deliver terawatts of electricity nearly anywhere. Proponents hope this super-hot rock approach can successfully resolve the escalating energy demands and woes of modern data centers.

articles.title: UN diplomats fail to reach agreement on killer robots
articles.summary: During a meeting in Geneva, United Nations diplomats attempted to establish regulations for autonomous weapons systems, often called killer robots. Following largely fruitless negotiations, representatives only agreed to begin discussing options moving forward.

articles.title: FBI and USDA systems reportedly targeted in cyberattacks
articles.summary: Reports indicate that both the United States Department of Agriculture and the FBI experienced cyberattacks. The FBI incident marks the second security breach targeting the agency in recent months, focusing on the National Crime Information Center.

articles.title: Chess.com expands into classic games like sudoku and mahjong
articles.summary: Following the launch of its gambling-free poker site earlier this year, Chess.com is introducing a new Classic Games platform. The hub will feature ten traditional games, including sudoku, mahjong, backgammon, checkers, and a Scrabble alternative.

articles.title: Modern genetics debunk race realism and innate differences
articles.summary: Recent scientific findings emphasize that modern genetics does not support pseudoscientific claims regarding innate racial differences in human intelligence. Experts point out that the concept of race realism holds no valid foundation in contemporary science.

articles.title: Trump FCC blocks California from enforcing phone service rules
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission has preempted state regulations that previously required companies like AT&T to maintain home phone service offerings. The decision explicitly blocks California from enforcing its own telecommunication mandates.

articles.title: Google updates search homepage to feature AI chat history
articles.summary: Google is rolling out a redesigned search homepage that removes the traditional search button and places a heavier focus on artificial intelligence. The updated interface makes it significantly easier for users to access their ongoing AI chat histories.

articles.title: Meta reconsiders net-zero goal due to AI data emissions
articles.summary: Meta is reportedly re-evaluating its 2030 sustainability targets as record-breaking carbon emissions generated by artificial intelligence data centers continue to rise. Observers are now watching to see if other major tech corporations will follow suit.

articles.title: Researcher exposes privacy risks in AI supply chain tests
articles.summary: A security researcher planted millions of trackable canary data points into the artificial intelligence supply chain to test information security. The experiment revealed a major privacy disaster, proving that sensitive data does not always remain private.

articles.title: Astronomers watch giant star swallow neighboring orbiter
articles.summary: A recent unexpected brightening in the night sky has been explained by astronomers as a giant star swallowing a smaller neighbor. Researchers observed the rare event as the smaller star orbited and was eventually consumed from within.

articles.title: Prisons permitted to jam contraband phones despite interference
articles.summary: Correctional facilities have been given approval to use technology to jam contraband mobile phones. However, the wireless industry association warns that these tests have demonstrated signal interference affecting nearby civilian phones up to two and a half miles away.

articles.title: Army delays detonating hazardous lead azide amid concerns
articles.summary: The U.S. Army has postponed plans to detonate a dangerously hazardous stockpile of lead azide following public fear and anger. Predictive modeling warned that a neurotoxic lead plume from the explosion could potentially travel up to 100 miles away.
